gloss: to write down, to record, to note

definitions.gloss: to write down, to record, to note, to document
definitions.explanation: To put something into writing for the purpose of recording or preserving information. More formal and literary than 書く (to write), with a nuance of documenting or making a record.

examples.japanese: {日記|にっき}に{思|おも}い{出|で}を{記|しる}した。
examples.english: I recorded my memories in a diary.

examples.japanese: {歴史書|れきししょ}にはこう{記|しる}されている。
examples.english: It is recorded as follows in the history book.

examples.japanese: {名前|なまえ}と{住所|じゅうしょ}を{用紙|ようし}に{記|しる}してください。
examples.english: Please write your name and address on the form.

notes:
USAGE:
{記|しる}す is a godan verb that is more formal and literary than {書|か}く (to write). It implies writing with the intent to document, preserve, or communicate important information. The passive form {記|しる}されている (is recorded/written) is very common, especially when citing historical or official documents.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {日記|にっき}に{記|しる}す: to record in a diary
- {歴史|れきし}に{記|しる}される: to be recorded in history
- {名前|なまえ}を{記|しる}す: to write one's name
- 〜と{記|しる}されている: it is written/recorded as ~
- {心|こころ}に{記|しる}す: to engrave in one's heart (to remember deeply)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{書|か}く (to write) is the everyday, general word. {記|しる}す is more formal and emphasizes the act of recording or documenting. {記録|きろく}する (to record) is similar but focuses more on systematic data recording. {記|しる}す has a more literary, personal quality.
